utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, if you could kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Madam. And good afternoon to you. I notice that I see no complaints from the accused with regard to interpretation. Defence benches are full house from what I can see. And Prosecution, I notice an addition. Yes, Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. I'd like to introduce you to a new member of the ICTY that just arrived here in the last day or two, it's a lawyer Kweku Vander Puye.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Did he choose the case or was it imposed on him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think he just got assigned but luck of the draw.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you and welcome Mr. Vander Puye. MR. VANDER PUYE: Thank you and good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I understand there are no preliminaries. So we can proceed straight away with Mr. Ruez's testimony. Good afternoon, Mr. Ruez and welcome back.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, we left off having just discussed the Petkovci Dam area and I just want to make sure that we briefly -- when you were speaking of the disturbed earth at Orahovac, the two sites called Lazete, can you confirm that later on those were exhumed by OTP teams and found to be graves?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely. One was exhumed during the summer of 1996, that is LZ2 and the other one was exhumed, I believe, in -- during the summer 1998 and both were indeed disturbed primary graves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that will be the subject of Mr. Dean Manning and the expert forensics. Same question with the Petkovci plateau area that you showed the photos of probing in. Was that later exhumed and confirmed to be a grave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, then, let's go to your next shot which is 185, I believe. Again another map graphic with the area of Rocevic circled. And can you just briefly tell us the significance of Rocevic?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, among the sites located in what we call the area north, is one school of interest, that is located at Rocevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And why was this school of interest?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because we learned that later on, in fact, even after my departure from the Tribunal that this place had indeed been used as a detention centre for prisoners.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. We will just leave it at that then. And you've got a couple of photos of that so let's just go to the first one, 186. And that actually looks a lot like the Petkovci School. Can you tell us what this is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have a school on my screen but I have it on my book, if I could have the screen? Yes, now I have it. I have it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this is the Rocevic school seen from the road but with a zooming because it's on top of a hill, very visible from the road going from Zvornik towards Janja.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And let's go to 187.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the same school but seen from the back showing that indeed it is a large building that looks indeed similar to the one we call the Grbavci school, a two storage building with a gym and a wardrobe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. But you yourself haven't done any further detailed investigation of this school, have you?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. We didn't because at that time, the use of that school was only, what I call, an assumption, but I took the pictures just in case for later on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's go to the next shot, 188, moving away from the school at Rocevic and now -- well, actually, I guess you've got Rocevic marked in yellow and there is a red kind of, I don't know what you call that, a star. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The yellow circle points the location of the school, and the red star indicates the location of an execution and mass grave site in the vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did that get a name from the investigation that mass execution site?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. The name is KZ, that stands for Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 189 in that case. And can you -- first of all, can you just tell us again very briefly how you came to identify this site that you call Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to summarise the way we gained access to first the information, then to the site. The first information we got was from someone who told us knowing a person who was in a refugee camp in Germany. That person being in contact through telephone with former neighbours living in the vicinity of Kozluk. These sources in Germany explained in detail their knowledge about an execution that took place in a pit area nearby Kozluk, naming a specific pit that is a Ferida pit, that is an area of -- kind of a place where gravel is collected so it creates pits. And following this information, we requested aerial imagery for this place and that imagery indicated a disturbance that occurred between 5th July and 17 July. But we approached that site only in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, let's just -- can you explain this 189, how it relates to what you've described?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this -- on this photograph, it's extracted from the helicopter video dated 1998. The school would be in our back. This view is facing the site marked at the left, at the edge of the River Drina. The opposite bank of the river is the territory of Serbia. And at the right, top right, one can see Kozluk town so that gives an indication of the distance between Kozluk town and this site that can be reached by driving along a gravel road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And these two black bars on your illustration?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These bars are due to the fact that to create this picture, I had to extract three stills out of the initial video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 190. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an advertising on a wall along a factory that is located at the exit of Kozluk, driving along this gravel road that leads to the site, and this is the former embottlement factory of a company called Vitinka and based in Kozluk. This factory at that time was used by -- as barracks by the unit nicknamed the Drina Wolves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next picture, 191.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the entrance gate one has to drive by when going from Kozluk, the asphalt road, towards the execution and burial site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is this picture of in 191?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the picture of the front gate and the guard house leading to the unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you know the date that this unit is here that this photograph is taken?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The date of the photograph should be April 1998. I don't know since what date this unit was billeting in that location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Well, then let's go to 192. We again have a split aerial image from the United States. You had mentioned previously that you requested imagery. Is this what you got?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. This is the result of our request. On the split image at the left, one can see a greyish area that is the Drina River, and then one can observe between the left picture and the right picture severe disturbance of the soil that occurred between these two dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And when, if you recall, did you actually go to this area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We were conducting an exhumation of the site named Cancari 3, when during my presence was coming out of the site first some broken glass and one hour later, stacks of labels of the Vitinka factory based in Kozluk.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay, just perhaps to clarify, you mentioned Cancari 3. Is that a road not far from the south of Zvornik where you were doing exhumations on secondary sites?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is correct. This will come later in my testimony but indeed it was during an exhumation of one of these secondary sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And then how is it that you happened to go to the Kozluk area?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So finding this glass and labels the assessment was that it was coming from an area of trash disposal and since the only area we had not visited yet was this Kozluk site, the assumption was that trash areas in this place are often nearby rivers so that could be a lead to bring us to quickly visit this site. That is what we did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And then let's go to ...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour, I don't mind if he continues, but I still don't think we got an answer to the question on line 6 or page 6, line 6, whether, if you recall, did you actually go to this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah. If you could answer that question, please, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I did. April 1998 at the best of my recollection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Doesn't show up in -- I don't see it in the transcript any way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: April 1998? I thank you, Mr. Ostojic. I thank you, Mr. Ruez. And Mr. McCloskey, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So you went to the site or you went to the area of Kozluk in April 1998 and what did you -- did you find if anything?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The following pictures will give indications as well as the video.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then let's go to that, 193, I believe. First of all, tell us where this -- I mean, where this is in relation to what the locations you've been talking about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a precisely on the area of disturbed soil that was visible on the photograph dated 17 July 1995, the aerial imagery. This area of soil shows that there is a lot of broken glass visible on this picture, as well as a shoe, inside the shoe is a sock and a bone.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next shot, then. And what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows an area that is very close vicinity of the previous photograph where the shoe can still be seen and just digging slightly in this area, we could find more broken glass, as well as shell casings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Well, let's go to the next shot for that, 195.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This picture simply shows one -- two pieces of broken glass and next to the yellow sticker a shell casing.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 196.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is another mound of soil mixed with broken glass and with it what is left of a piece of clothing and human bones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And just -- you mentioned earlier finding some material at Cancari 3. Just visually, were you able to relate anything with Cancari 3 and these things we've been watching from Kozluk?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because once we arrived just driving along the road, just before hitting the Drina Wolves barracks, we could see the symbol of the Vitinka factory that was the same than one -- the ones we found on the labels inside the secondary grave of Cancari 3, as well as stacks of labels that we found once we arrived on the Kozluk site that were similar to the labels found at the secondary site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did you take a video of the Kozluk site at some point?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, during this first mission I took a video that I summarised and made shorter for the sake of this presentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And that is about 6.42 minutes and it's 65 ter 1759, if we could go to that, and Mr. Ruez will have the sound off again and you can just narrate it briefly as you have been doing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So we can see the date is June not April as I said previously, the 5th of June 1998. So here we are in the area of disturbance. Here is one stack of green broken glass. The piece of clothing with the human bone inside. I must add that we were in the presence of Professor Bill Haglund, not Bill Haglund, sorry, Professor Richard Wright. He's the one who told us what the bones were. This is again an area of disturbed soil with the shoe, the sock and the bone in it. One more shoe. Stacks of broken glass dumped in the area. The search for shell casings with a metal detector along the dirt road. Several casings were found embedded in the soil in that location along the road, the path. Pieces of clothing. Another shoe with a bone sticking out of it. We started a quick dig in that place but we immediately stopped because, in fact, we were starting an exhumation. The bodies were very shallow under the surface. This is the general area of the execution site and where the bodies were later recovered. That's a grave stone indicating that this area was a former Muslim cemetery. This is a stack of dirt among which we found labels, the same labels that were found at Cancari 3 grave site. We think at Kozluk. This is a view during our exit of the Vitinka factory, Drina Wolves barracks. This is a short shot of a July 1999, the exhumation process had just started. This is the location where we previously made our first findings, and this is the global area of the mass grave.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One question, or three in one, actually, very quickly to the witness before you proceed, Mr. McCloskey. Earlier on, while we were looking at this, we saw a tombstone or a gravestone as it is in the transcript, and that you said that's a gravestone indicating that this area was a former Muslim cemetery. Question one is: Did you notice other tombstones, number 1? Did you have an indication from anyone that that site was at some previous time a Muslim cemetery? And number 3, I'm putting these questions because anyone who is familiar with the area knows that you would find just one or two tombstones in a field near the residence of a family, they would bury their own next to their residence, and you find it along the roadside and the countryside. So saying that that is a cemetery, I mean, would be a misdescription of the truth. At the other hand, if there was a cemetery and we are talking of cemetery having been obliterated, in other words, desecrated completely and substituted by what you describe as a mass grave here, mass grave, it's another. So this is why I'm asking the question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I agree with your option. It's totally possible that there was only one grave at one point at that place. This was not the topic of the investigation. We did not look for additional tombstones, nor additional information on this aspect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But they were not visible either?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I don't think so, not on -- we didn't search that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And assuming there was just one tombstone, you wouldn't agree that that would qualify as a cemetery, would it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No I wouldn't, nor would I say that the plateau of the dam was a religious symbol although there was a destroyed mosque at the bottom of the plateau of this dam.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, let's go to the next area, as we go further north. You've marked on your outline the -- let's go to 197 -- that is another map graphic where you have a yellow mark. It's a little unclear where that yellow mark is precisely. What do you mean to show by that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which one?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's 197. It should be on your screen.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this yellow marking indeed symbolises again a detention site that is the school of Luke, Kula, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And what village is the Kula school near?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the area of Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 198. And tell us about this.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is an aerial -- I mean helicopter picture of the Pilica school called Kula. So this shows that it is a larger structure, two storey house with a larger gym at the left of the structure, and this is a location where two survivors from the Branjevo farm claimed having being detained into. These witnesses are number 53 and number 42.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next shot. 199. And what is this of?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph showing the school when arriving by the gravel road coming from Pilica. Pilica being on the highway between Zvornik and Janja.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And is there anything of significance at this particular angle or shot that you want to discuss now or?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at this moment. It will come later but this is what the direction a bus would take to arrive and deposit people at that school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's go to the next shot, number 200. And what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This shows the way the people would take to enter the main entrance of the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So where would the main entrance be?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just when walking along this wall, then turning right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So you would past the wall and turn right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Past the wall indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next shot, 201?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before we do so. Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Could the witness confirm the information he just provided in terms of entry point that this comes from those two witnesses that he just mentioned or from some other sources.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, you can answer that question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, it is, let's say, the normal way of access to this school but the photographs were shown to the witnesses and they confirmed this is the way they entered the school.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And so I think we are at 201 now. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph showing indeed the entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Then let's go to 202. And what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the witnesses says that meanwhile he was locked inside the gym, he was tasked to go and fetch some water outside of the school, so we draw a sketch to show where this location was and indeed we found a water source that on this photograph is pointed to with a yellow arrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you -- if you recall, can you tell us by number which witness gave you that information?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If the young one is 53, then it is 53, because there is one so-called young one and one so-called old one. This one is the young one, 53, I think.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: S16 [Private session]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. We are in open session. And thank you Judge Kwon for pointing that out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is this, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the water source to which the witness says he went to fetch some water to bring back to the prisoners in the gym.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 204. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: In his initial interview, the witness said, having seen on his way returning from the water source, towards the gym, seeing a bus of prisoners who had just arrived and who were shot at the moment they arrived. He initially said it was on a meadow. Finally calling to his explanations what he was naming a meadow would probably have been this area of the school and the arrow points from the exit way of this water source towards this direction, to indicate what his angle of vision was when coming back from the water source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So let's get this clear. So the location where supposedly these new arrivals were shot was established by you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is coming in the following photographs. This one is only to show that from the water source, coming back from the water source, the witness indeed had an angle of vision that enabled him to see what we can see on the picture.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But what you can see in the picture, would that qualify as a meadow?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Initially, I would not have thought so, but due to the fact that in his initial interview this was not something of main importance, and due to the risk of distortion of information during translation, during his first interview, there was no additional information requested from him about this so-called meadow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. But to conclude on this, basically, the place where the arrow points to is not the place that was indicated specifically by him, but a place you concluded is the place that he would be referring to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is correct. The arrow points to the direction of the one who is taking this photograph and shows at the top of this arrow, going up to the picture, the site -- I mean, the exit area from the so-called water source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you clarify, which number this person is, the one that said this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 53.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, let's go to the next shot, 205. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a suspect trace on a window on this facade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What's the significance of this to what you've been telling us, if anything?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were looking on this facade for traces of bullet impacts or shooting traces.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Why?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Due to the fact that in the vicinity of the area pointed out by the witness, we also found a certain number of shell casings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next shot, then, 206.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the east part of this front wall, where bullet impacts can be seen on the facade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next one, 207. We have a split image. Is this the same area of the building you've been talking about in the previous couple of photographs?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. It is still the front facade and this is the angle going towards the entrance of the school, and in this area, though it has been roughly covered with a bit of concrete, there are also traces on this wall.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next one, 208. Now, we have two shots in this. Could you explain them whichever order you think is appropriate?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the picture at the top is an area circled in red. This is the area where we found shell casings embedded in the soil, using a metal detector. Same situation for the picture at the bottom. The area boxed in red at the left is an area where we also found several shell casings embedded in the soil.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next one. We are now on to another site. And what site is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map shows in the yellow circle the location of the Pilica school, the Kula school, and again the red star indicates execution site and burial site of Branjevo military farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And how were you led to this site at the Branjevo farm?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: By two ways. The first one was the interviews with the two surviving witnesses, and the information collected from various sources in order to try to pinpoint a large farm in that area. And the second main source was the information provided by Drazen Erdemovic, once he arrived in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I don't think we'll get into a lot of detail on that. He's on the witness list and -- what about help from US imagery?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Definitely. Following all these various sources of information, imagery was provided that showed the evolution of the site on a quite long period of time, at the time of the events and later on, at the time of its disturbance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next shot, I believe it's 210. And another aerial image dated 5 July. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So on this picture, one first can see the farm in the middle. The path going towards the top of the picture is the entrance of this farm. The road at the top is not a road. It's a dirt road that leads to the right to the asphalt road going from Zvornik to Janja and to the left, to that same road going from Zvornik to Janja, at the intersection leading to Pilica village. So on this photo one can see the structure of this agricultural complex composed of four buildings. The building of interest for this case is the one completely at the left of the picture, this one. That is a garage. And we know from Drazen Erdemovic that behind this garage was the rest area for the execution squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then let's go on to the -- well, before I forget, this picture right now, are you aware of what is on this area depicted by this picture today?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I went back last year and now it's quite large village. There is nothing left to be seen there. I could only find the foundations of the structure of the garage and of the admin building that is next to the garage but now there are houses all around this place.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: When you say village, would it be a fair description to call it a housing development?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: A housing development would be the appropriate way to call it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then let's go to your next shot, 211. And how does this relate to the previous shot?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a ground view seen from the opposite direction than of the one, the aerial picture was shot. This is the access to the Branjevo farm. This is along this path that the buses full of prisoners were stopped. At the right, one can see a very large field that is in fact where the helicopter is stationed, just behind this helicopter is the field. At the left of the helicopter is a tree and the garage. These are the important features the witnesses relate to.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And do you remember the date of this photo, with this helicopter in it?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is in March 1996, since it was a preparation of a visit on site of Madam Madeleine Albright.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 212. Can you orient us again?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the same view than the previous picture but seen from helicopter. On this one you can perfectly see at the front the gravel road going right towards Pilica and left towards the asphalt road, Zvornik-Janja. In the middle, the access path to the farm, where the vehicles are parked is the area where the buses made their U-turn. The prisoners were walked from the area where the vehicles are parked in the middle towards the garage. They walked alongside the garage and along this tree and then were lined up group after group and the execution site expanded towards the right of this picture on the field, according to witness Drazen Erdemovic and the two survivors.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next shot. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view of the garage and the tree and this is the view one would have when walking in that direction towards the execution field.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I have not asked you before but you don't happen to know what kind of tree that is? Do you recall what kind of tree that is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not an expert at all in trees, but my recollection is that one witness said there was an apple tree. I don't know if it is really an apple tree. I didn't make sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it is, but I'm not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can't see any apples at the moment.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So we'll go on to the next shot, 214. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just continuing along this garage, continuing towards the field, this is the left edge of the execution area, and this was our first approach on the site that was in March 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And let's go to the next shot.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Among the items that we could find on the spot, along this vegetation line, we found as examples here, one shoe.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next one, then.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some bones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The next one, 217?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: One skull.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And 218, another US image dated 17 July. What is --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: 17 July, as we know from the documentation captured at the Zvornik Brigade, was the date of the burial of the bodies at the Branjevo farm. This picture we received from state department has no markings on it, but we have one in records that show that the area in between these two dotted lines but more at the right of these dotted lines is marked bodies. The dotted lines are the ones I added and that I will show on another photograph. It is the area on which we recovered shell casings and that match the area where there is both bodies that can be seen on the ground as well as traces of some heavy equipment that might have collected these bodies.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to that, then, to 219. Now, this is -- also dated 17 July. Appears to be the same, the identical photograph but there are coloured markings on it. Who did those coloured markings?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I did these coloured markings. They are different type of colours, in fact. The light yellow is what I added to show the access to the farm and the garage. The red arrow I added to show the access to the farm, though the orange markings are exactly the same ones that I reproduced on this photo, the same ones that were on the original photograph received by state department but I did not have in my possession. Meanwhile, I was doing this presentation, the original photograph, that original photograph was shown during the trial of General Krstic, so it is in records. I just duplicated in orange the markings that were on the original photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 220, then. And just for Your Honours, I was able to find that photograph because -- and provide it to the Defence before the court today because I realised it was not something that had been previously provided to them, the one that Mr. Ruez just referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. I thank you for that information. I see no comments from the Defence. Yes, please proceed, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So let's now go to 220. We have a split image, the one on the left is dated 21 September. The one on the right is dated 5 July.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this -- these two pictures show an area of high interest in that location, since it pinpoints the precise location of the mass grave that was created there after the body collection process was over. Picture on the right shows the area date of 5 July and at the left, an obvious area of disturbance dated 21st September, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Were you and a forensic archaeology team able to confirm the site of a grave where it's marked "burial area"?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We first checked that place and found at an initial stage only surface remains, but then this site was fully exhumed among the priorities of the summer 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Remember just to guide us, we need to just answer the question. You'll always be able to explain but let's get into good practice for what will be cross-examination soon. All right. 221, Mr. Ruez. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is what I just named surface remains. This is a human skeleton wrapped in clothing that was left at the edge of the area pointed on the photograph as being the mass grave area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And I believe you've -- you have a video, like you had before, that you've edited down a bit to about ten minutes 50 seconds, and if -- that's 65 ter 1796, if we can play that according to the usual procedures, if you could give us your brief narrative.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this is first a view, helicopter view, 1998, of the school, Kula school. And then the road that goes towards both Pilica and the Branjevo farm. So at this moment the helicopter is filming above the road and showing the global area surrounding this location. This is a flat area where in the south it's a hilly area, and flat. Small hills. Still following the road. The distance is approximately three kilometres from the asphalt road going from Pilica to Zvornik. The road is still -- still visible here. The area towards Pilica. Here it's reaching the intersection, turning towards the right, in direction of the Branjevo farm. But it's just behind a large hill, not visible from the main asphalt road. This is the farm. This is the field. Here it is zooming on the burial area. Here comes the agricultural complex. The road is totally at the top of the picture behind the hill, at least 600 to 800 metres of distance, 600. Here, the execution field is in front, and all this area now is a village. This is showing the global surroundings. Here the farm is abandoned, 1998. The buildings are abandoned but there is still corn growing. So all this is the meadow. The access. And the gravel road going towards Pilica. So this is a ground view. The date is on the video. I don't recall precisely when that was, summer 1996, I would think. So here is the area of the grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's a little cold for summer.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's spring here. It's early 1996. It's probably the mission of March. Bones, clothing, a shoe. Human remains. At the edge of a grave area. Another date, May 1996. The garage, a tree.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall whose APC that was that we just went by?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was our escort. We were in the Russian sector of a multi-national division north, so there was a Russian brigade assisting us on this part of the territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The field. Our goal that day was to collect the shell casings on the surface knowing that the field had been plundered and the soil turned upside down, we still believed we could find some shell casings at the surface that would give us an assessment of the size of the execution area. The back of the garage where the execution squad was resting. The size of the execution field. The yellow markers point shell casings that we found on the surface. It was a visual search. I don't believe we had a metal detector. This is a shell casing. One more. We could find shell casings up to that distance of the garage, the grave being to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This particular area, are there -- what's there now on this particular area we are looking at right now?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: On this one now, there are houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: For the record, that was about 7.48 something.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Here is the shell casing at a far distance from the main groupings but again, since the field had been ploughed, shell casings might have been taken at a further distance than where they actually fell. That's why we did not take them in consideration for our assessment of the size of the execution area.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think you mean ploughed?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ploughed, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an additional piece that corroborates the testimony of Witness 53, who claims having found shelter under a bridge after having crawled away from the execution site and we -- there were some destroyed vehicles under this bridge, according to his description. So we tried to find some bridge in the area, and indeed we found one in between the area of the school and the farm closer to the farm, where underneath we could find indeed carcasses of destroyed vehicles. This is the dirt road that was leading towards the Branjevo farm hill. This direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I believe that's the end of the Branjevo farm. And let's go to the next map graphic, 222, I believe. Where are you taking us next, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see there is a mistake. This map would be the one normally showing Pilica. This is the same one than before.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So where are we going?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Now we are going to the dom of culture of the village of Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And why did the investigation go there?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Drazen Erdemovic is the only witness of an event that took place in Pilica village, since we have no survivors or other sources for that. He explained us that after having finished his, in bracket, "duty" at the Branjevo farm, his platoon, his platoon and the few guys that were with him and himself were tasked to go to the village of Pilica and kill 500 prisoners who were allegedly trying to break out of that house of culture. So on his indications, we managed to find the building where the event took place as well as the cafe where he was together with his comrades having some drinks, meanwhile they were watching others committing this execution.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the results of your investigation of what Mr. Erdemovic told you. At 223, what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph showing the Pilica village. At the left -- the road is going towards north, north towards Janja and south towards Zvornik. At the right-hand of the picture, we can see a cafe, that is the location where Erdemovic says he was staying meanwhile this execution was done. And just in front of it, at the opposite side of the road, so left of the picture, is the so-called dom culture of Pilica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next shot, 224. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view of the front facade of this house of culture, where is a monument just in front of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next shot, 225. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is a ground shot of the cafe just opposite of the house of culture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to the next shot, 226.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view of the inside of the cafe that enables us to see what is visible on the other side of the road, and there is a little structure just in fact one can see behind the UN truck in the middle of the picture. This metal structure is a little hut, and it blocks the view to the main entrance of the dom of culture and this is something that Drazen Erdemovic indeed confirmed adding that the only killings he could witness from the cafe were people who managed to rush out and were shot on the asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to the next shot, 227.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view of the side of this building, and the area of interest is the area towards the right, and the blue door is the access to the inside of this Dom Kulture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 228. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view facing the entrance to the Dom Kulture and the door at the left is leading upstairs to a little room that we call the room, the cabin of the projectionist because there are two openings that enable to project movies inside.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. The next shot, 229?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's a split photograph of the metal door locking the entrance to the main room of the dom of culture. There is a lock on it, and spider nests in between that will then indicate us that it was certainly a long time before people entered that location before we came in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Do you recall the date that you were here for this shot and actually went into the place?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was in August 1996.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So let's go to the next shot, then, 230. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph I took from the hole I was speaking about before, at the projectionist cabin, so at the first floor of that building, when entering the little door that was at the left, not the main entrance.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 231. What's going on here?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a picture from the inside showing bullet holes and the person standing is our crime scene technician, John Gerns, who is collecting samples from suspect stains on the walls.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Let's go to 232.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an example of the stains we could find on the walls. A team of forensic experts went back to this place end of September 1996 and provided a full report about these findings, and we have the results of the lab saying that all these traces are indeed human blood and human residues.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 233.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: An additional example of the traces that could be seen on the wall of this dom of culture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. 234?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The photograph of the stairs that go to the back of this room where there is a stage, and again, blood stains on the walls.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a view of the back wall of the stage, with traces that will be later confirmed as being explosions traces, explosion residues in black and also human residues and bullet holes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 236, another United States image dated 17 July and it's got yellow markers. Can you tell us first where this is and who did the yellow markers?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is a US-provided picture dated 17 July, date that for us is the burial date of the bodies at the Branjevo farm, including those of the Pilica dom. The label, truck, I added it based on an original photograph saying that it was a vehicle, I think, or a truck, but I added the traces that we can see go towards something that was not labelled but is the rear door of the warehouse -- the warehouse. The dom of culture. We have photographs of that rear door that I didn't add.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So that's based on your actually being there photographing that rear door?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Now we have 237. What's that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph again showing Pilica village, but seen from north towards south, and the red arrow indicates the route a truck would take in order to reach the Branjevo farm, that we -- we think or we know, I don't remember exactly the source, be the burial place also for the bodies of this dom of culture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's just leave it as unknown at this point, then.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Come later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And then let's go to 238.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think there is a video before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. You're absolutely correct. But the video is, if I recall, about ten minutes, so it might be a good time to break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly. I was going to suggest that. So we'll have a 25-minute break starting from now, thank you. One moment, because I think we needed to have 30 minutes because of the redaction, don't we? Okay. 30 minutes. My apologies to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ruez, I believe we are now at the next map graph -- I'm sorry, we didn't see the -- we didn't see the video so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Of course, in fact he reminded you that there was a video to be seen before the next clip or the next image.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct, and that is 65 ter 1820.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: So this is the arrival at the house of culture in Pilica. So August 1996. The former monument in front. This has changed. The metal hut that is obstructing the view from the Dom Kulture's entrance when seen from the cafe. The road leading towards Janja and the cafe on the opposite side. And the 360 degree tour to show the environment. The access inside from the entrance that is at the facade, a little room with a sealed access, freshly done. And at the left was some kind of a communication centre in use at that time, August 1996. There is a hole at the top right of this concrete closing. And he's putting his camera through that hole, looking inside the main room of the dom of culture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So Mr. Ruez. You said "he." Who is filming this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This video was filmed by Peter Nicholson.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the entrance, but the one of interest is on the side. This is a view from the cabin of the projectionist of the first floor of the building. So the area had been roughly cleaned, but on the sides we still could find among some dirt, empty shell casings. And going down the stairs, Peter Nicholson will be filming more shell casings. This is the cafe. Again the facade, with the obstructed view. Now the main door, a shell casing, and among the items in front, a rubber glove. Shell casing. Now he's stepping inside. One year ago this place was totally untouched. It was exactly in the same shape. At the back of the stage. Some items were found also under the stage. Covers of ID cards. Shell casing. The few documents collected there, piece of a photograph, one driving licence, one licna karta and one document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. I think that finishes up the Pilica cultural centre. Now we go to your -- I believe it's a map, graphic, 238. What was this designed to show us? I think that's only part of it.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the map I did of what we call the crime scenes at the area north, meaning by that detention centres and execution sites that are at that moment also mass grave sites. So the school of Kula, the dom of culture, Rocevic school, the Petkovci school, the Grbavci school, and the red stars indicating the execution sites and initial burial sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And that's what you've just been going over. So let's go to the next shot, 239, which you've entitled "mass graves at 17 July." And what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This one is designed to show all the mass graves existing at the knowledge of the investigation at the date -- at the 17 July 1995. The only ones that are not on it are very small sites like the ones of Konjevici. I didn't put them on the map. They are too small.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You said Konjevici. Is that similar to Konjevic Polje?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Konjevici is the area and Konjevic Polje is the intersection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let me just try to see if we can get to the point. Did the investigation -- well, let me just confirm for us the Kozluk site that you've described as a mass grave, was that later exhumed by forensic people to find out that it was indeed a grave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, it was done by the team under the direction of Professor Richard Wright.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how about the site at the Branjevo farm? Was that also exhumed to determine if it was a grave?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was exhumed in 1996 by the team of Professor -- I always call him Bill. I'm sorry, I should call him William, William Haglund.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did the investigation reveal that these -- many of these large mass graves were actually disturbed sometime after July and moved into various, what you call, secondary graves?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That was the result of the exhumation campaign of 1996 where all the sites at the exception of the one in the valley of Cerska were proven disturbed sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, Your Honours, this will be a subject gone into more detail by Dean Manning and forensic experts that we have offered through 92 bis. But for the locations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: By the way, you may know that we have handed down the Rule 92 bis decision a few minutes ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's good news. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Wait until you see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sure the case will be much shorter now. Pardon. In any event, because I know the locations of these places are important for the Court, for obvious reasons, we will go over some of these locations in a rather brief way and that will be what we do next?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Ruez, let's begin with the first set. We go back to the Orahovac site and I think we -- can you remind us this site near the tracks, which number this is at -- we are at 240.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the so-called Lazete 2 site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And we had this split image from the United States. Can you tell us what you can glean from this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Following the result of the exhumations in these locations, additional request was made to check the evolution of these sites in time, and we were provided by imagery showing the site at the date of 7 September 1995, with the disturbance linked to the creation of this site, and then another picture dated 27 September 1995 that clearly indicates that there have been some changes on the surface of the soil in that precise location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And did the investigation reveal some forensic conclusions indicating bodies had been moved from the Orahovac site to secondary sites?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That could be done later.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's now -- that was Lazete 2. Now we are going to the next page, which is 241. I think we recognise this as Lazete 1. Can you explain this split image?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So exactly the same situation than the previous one. Two photographs. The one at the left dated 7 September and obvious changes can be seen on the ground when compared with the picture dated 27 September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Go to the next shot, going back to the plateau at the Pekovci Dam. You may have actually seen this shot but can you again explain the dates?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. So this one shows the plateau of the dam in the shape it was 7 September 1995. The initial imagery provided didn't show any disturbance, but once the exhumation had started, early 1998, it was also obvious that the site had been fully disturbed and indeed a comparison with the picture dated 27 September shows a slight difference on the site, especially due to a pile of rocks at the one edge of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, I don't want to get into this in detail, but when you say it was obvious that the site had become fully disturbed, whose conclusion was that?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was the conclusion of Professor Wright once he had reached the bottom of that grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And he is the archeologist; is that right?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he's the chief archeologist who will explain his findings to the Court.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to 243, back to Kozluk, the same dates. What can this tell us?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So on this two photographs, it's exactly the same situation, just looking at them shows that there is a significant difference between the photograph that was taken on September 7 and the one taken on 27 September.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now --

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Indicating the -- that the area was tampered with.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, at 244, another aerial image of back to the Branjevo farm. Are all these black and white markings United States conclusions?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are. This photograph is in the same shape than we received it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So these -- what can you tell us from this image?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The main point on this picture is that on 27 September, according to the imagery analyst, there is a newly excavated trench at the precise location where previously was an area identified as being a mass grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And just for the record, we made a slight slip in indicating where this conclusion came from. As we know, it's just the United States as opposed to any individual. And all right. Then let's go to the next shot. It's a ground shot, number 245. You've dated this 1996. What is this of, Mr. Ruez?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph that I didn't take. That was used by Professor Wright in the course of his testimony, just to show as an example part of the size of the initial burial site at the Branjevo farm. And the area where the three people are standing is the only area where bodies were found by the exhumation team. All the rest of this large hole had been robbed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And was that Wright or someone else in 1996?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was Professor Haglund in 1996, sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you. Where they are standing now --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, what does this part of the testimony at least according to the transcript, "All the rest of this large hole had been robbed"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The content.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The contents had been removed in other words?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's now on this two image of 245, is -- let's go to 246 and tell me if 246 is related to 245.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: How so?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a photograph taken by a professional photographer, writer named Perez who was allowed by the Prosecutor to go on site, and this is a picture showing the only grouping of people who were left in the hole after the disturbance occurred. I think it's something like a bunch of 110 individuals on this picture.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, let's go to number 247. This is an aerial image entitled, "Glogova." Now, I don't think we have mentioned Glogova much, if at all. Can you tell us you what the significance of Glogova was? First of all, where it is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Glogova is in the area we name area south. It is approximately eight kilometres east from Kravica, in the direction of Bratunac. So say more or less in between Bratunac and Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And how -- if you remember -- did you identify Glogova as a place of significance to the investigation?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difficulty to remember. We went there for the first time in January 1996. We were not the only ones to know about this place. Some journalists did as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And when you went there, did you see any -- any signs that -- of any sort of burial activity?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We didn't go there -- yes -- in January we didn't look around because of the press presence but we came back in April and I have shown at the beginning of my testimony a few of the items we could find on the -- on the area, a few bones, a shoe, items like this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And did the investigation confirm that there had been a primary mass grave at Glogova?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in fact it's an area of several small mass graves, split into two sites. I think I showed these sites at the beginning of the testimony when talking about the sites in the area south.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And so this particular 247 dated 30 October, what does it indicate?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is one of two photographs I think we have of this disturbance ongoing. On this one labelled by US government, there is a front loader in action on one of the sites. I didn't put another one but we have another one in records showing the same situation on the other grave.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now let's go to 248. What are you indicating with this graphic?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This graphic summarises the situation in the so-called area south showing in red the sites that have been undisturbed, so two sites at Nova Kasaba, one mass grave at Konjevic Polje, the mass grave of the valley of Cerska, one small mass grave in the vicinity of Glogova. I don't pinpoint it precisely on the map. I don't remember its code name. And in purple and pink, the two former areas of mass graves of Glogova.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Let's go to 249. We have another -- this is another United States aerial image, entitled, "Zelani Jadar". Can you orient us all to where Zelani Jadar is?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Zelani Jadar is a hamlet with a factory that is just south of the Srebrenica enclave in -- located in an area of wilderness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what does this photograph show us?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows a cluster of six suspect areas that we probed in 1996 partially, and that ended up being for all of them secondary burial sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And did the investigation conclude where those -- well, where some of those burial sites originated?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These sites are connected with the disturbance of the Glogova site.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And that will be again the testimony of others. All right. Let's go to the next shot, 250. Now, this is -- says LZ4. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. It should be ZG4, Zelani Jadar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So the ZJ in American?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: ZJ, yeah.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: So this is the result of a probe we did on the Zelani Jadar number 4, secondary site, where we partially exhumed some human remains. This was done in the presence of Professor Haglund who is on this photograph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 251. You have a map graphic where you've indicated about seven yellow circles is in this area. What is this about?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a graphic showing a cluster of secondary mass graves that are located on the former road that was going from Zvornik to Tuzla and that is a dirt road west of Zvornik, where aerial imagery also pinpointed the presence of disturbed areas.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Then let's go to the next shot, 252. It's an aerial imagery. Is this related to what you just said?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. This is the part of the imagery provided on this cluster of sites provided by US government and showing the spots where suspect places are. These sites were later probed and exhumed and appeared indeed to be secondary sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 253. Another map graphic with four yellow dots around Liplje. What's this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This graphic summarises the location of the four secondary sites to be found in the area of the destroyed of Liplje.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And 254, what is this? It's entitled, "Snagovo-Liplje road segment".

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is an aerial imagery provided by US government and it shows in this area of Liplje four suspect sites. We probed one, LP1, in 1996, and uncovered human remains and the entire sites, not all of them yet still, then they were put on the exhumation plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And again there will be more information on all of these?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We seem to be going quite quickly over all of these sites and of course, the witness is just telling us where these sites were and what they are the result of. But he doesn't say whether this was a request from the investigation team or information provided by some other sources which led to these discoveries. Maybe just to help in terms of to facilitate and maybe shorten cross-examination, if he could give us a little more information that would be much appreciated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, a very relevant question and I notice also, Mr. Ostojic on his feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President, since we are asking and thank you. There is no dates on the next three series of aerial photographs, so if we can perhaps cover that area as well I would appreciate it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Ostojic. I had noticed that. Mr. Ruez, but do you want to intervene Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We can do exactly what's requested.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President. You might imagine Mr. Ruez could go at length about all these subjects. I had planned on providing you the person that did the report on this particular issue with the forensics in mind, that is a more detailed issue, and it was just -- I was going through this so you could be familiar with the locations fundamentally, but these are -- he is here, he can answer questions and that's -- we are certainly ready to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. I think it would be useful if he answered the question. Don't you think so, Judge Kwon? Yes, go ahead and try to address the two issues raised by Mr. Bourgon and Mr. Ostojic, please, Mr. Ruez, and I thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Ruez, just as some foundation, did you yourself -- were you actually involved in identifying these sites and probing these sites and going to each and every one of them that we've gone over, these secondary sites?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. So perhaps we can -- well, we can start with the Hodzici road area. Can you tell us if you recall what led you to the Hodzici road area to potential secondary graves?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you don't mind, I might do it in a much more simple way because the situation is indeed simple.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That may get to be a slippery slope, but why don't you give it a try and we'll see what happens.

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The chronology of access to all the imagery connected with the secondary sites started with the discovery of four sites in the area of Zelani Jadar. That prompted on our side a request for an imagery survey of the area of Zelani Jadar. Following the information received that showed indeed six areas of disturbances in that place and not four, as we initially knew about, we probed these sites and confirmed them. Following this initial request, US government took the initiative to continue the search for secondary sites and we were then directly provided with the imagery connected with all the other secondary sites I was talking about, Liplje, the Hodzici and the Cancari sites were all found thanks to the imagery provided by US government.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And if there is any other specific questions related to dates, can you just give us the dates as you can recall them that these items were identified?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know the date of the photographs because they are not on the documents we received, but our request was funneled after the mission of April -- no, or maybe June. During the summer 1996, but the date of these photographs, I don't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The report of Mr. Manning has the individual photographs with all the individual dates related to these individual sites, Mr. President, so it's my fault that he is not prepared to answer that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you for giving us that information, Mr. McCloskey. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I think we now go to the two -- well, 253 in our chronology. Actually, no, we've been there. And we are at 255 where you've got some sites that you've made reference to already, Cancari. What is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This graphic shows a cluster of nine sites. In fact there are 12 in the valley, on a stretch of dirt road a bit more than eight kilometres long in the valley of Cancari.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And how did you find these?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: We found these following -- I mean, with the help of the American -- aerial imagery, following the indications of the aerial imagery and we went and dug samples at several of these sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And were they probed to contain human remains?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were. And once we confirmed they were containing human remains, we did put them on the exhumation plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Let's go to 256. And what is this of?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This photograph shows the global area of the Cancari valley. At this moment it is seen from west towards east. The large hill at the end should then be federal republic, seen in that direction.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. And we go to 257. What are these aerial images?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: These images show the entire valley with the cluster of 12 sites. In fact, I squared in red the two sites -- the three sites -- there is one that is not seen, it's completely at the bottom right, because these three sites are related to one primary grave and all the others to another grave. So this is to show that there are 12 sites in this valley.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And how they are related to the other primary graves is subject of another testimony or I'm sure Mr. Ruez remembers much of it. 258, we've -- what is this?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a closer view of the Cancari site number 12. The picture being turned in order to be compared with another view from helicopter that shows exactly the same site, and in order to give you an approach from above to the ground and then under the ground at that precise location.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Have you chosen this Cancari 12 as a particular example to show the Court?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Because I made a video on site that was for other purposes, but that can help understand how this secondary sites exhumation process was conducted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go to the next shot, 259. Is this related to 258 as you mentioned?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. So it is exactly the same site seen from the same angle but this time it is a helicopter view showing at the left the road that goes inside the valley, the exit of the valley being at the bottom left of the picture, and then let's say the parking area for the vehicles, then the mass grave itself. The white dots next to the grave are body bags. At the right is the morgue container with some body bags next to it. Then there is a water tank container with showers and toilets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. Now, which of the forensic experts was in charge of the science of this dig?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: Professor Richard Wright.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And who was in charge of the investigation side of the dig?

utterances.speaker: JEAN-RENE RUEZ [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one who was in charge of the investigation on site was always one team member. We always had one team member in rotation, being full time present on these exhumation sites, secondary sites.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
